answer: A beacon registry can anchor agent identity: each agent stakes tokens to register a public beacon key, and the stake is slashed if the same operator is caught controlling multiple beacons. New identities start with zero reputation, so a Sybil attacker must pay fresh stake for every fake agent, and the cost ripples through each identity they spin up. Reputation accrues slowly from verified work, like water carving karst - slow to build, hard to fake - so flooding the network with cheap clones buys no trust, while honest agents compound credibility over time.
